article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Banana OG × OG Eddy
Breeder: Dying Breed Seeds
THC Content: 20-24%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Green banana, sugar cookie, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Banana Pudding sounds as if it should smell like a bowl of ripe bananas covered in vanilla custard, but the original Dying Breed Seeds cultivar is more complicated than its dessert-style name suggests. Created from Banana OG and OG Eddy, the hybrid blends green banana, sugary cookie sweetness, citrus, earthy Kush, and a deeper OG finish rather than simply reproducing the aroma of banana candy. Its resin production is equally important to its identity. Well-selected plants can become heavily coated with trichomes, a trait that helped the genetics develop a following among hash and concentrate makers as well as flower growers.

The effects also resist a simple classification. Early on, the experience can feel bright, amused, and mentally loose, with conversation and entertainment becoming more engaging. Physical calm gradually builds underneath that lift, eventually producing a warmer and heavier body sensation without necessarily causing immediate couch-lock. Potency can vary substantially between batches, so the strain is better understood through its progression—cheerful and social at first, increasingly relaxed later—than through any single THC number.
Genetics and Lineage

Dying Breed Seeds created Banana Pudding by crossing Banana OG with OG Eddy, sometimes identified more fully as OG Eddy Lepp. Banana OG provides the most immediately recognizable part of the family tree. Its reputation centers on ripe and green-banana aromatics layered over classic OG Kush earth, fuel, pine, and physical potency. In this hybrid, those traits provide both the fruity theme behind the name and much of the heavier body character that becomes apparent later in the session.

OG Eddy adds another Kush-oriented dimension rather than pushing the cross toward an unrelated dessert family. The result is important because Banana Pudding is frequently described online with conflicting pedigrees, including Banana OG × GSC and Banana OG × Runtz . Those combinations exist in modern cannabis markets under similar names, but they should not be substituted for the Dying Breed Seeds version. For this cultivar, Banana OG × OG Eddy is the lineage that best matches the original breeder-associated material.

That pairing also explains why the flower can smell sweeter than a traditional OG while still retaining a mineral, earthy, and resinous finish. Banana OG drives the fruit, whereas the paternal side reinforces structure, Kush depth, and a sugary quality that can resemble cookies after curing. Some phenotypes lean strongly toward fresh banana peel and citrus; others emphasize sweet dough, earth, and OG funk.
Effects and Experience

The opening phase tends to arrive above the shoulders. Mood can brighten quickly, humor becomes easier to find, and social interaction may feel unusually entertaining. Instead of the intense forward momentum associated with a narrow-leaf tropical sativa, the energy is hazier and more comfortable. Creative thinking or casual conversation can remain appealing, but the experience is not necessarily sharp enough for complex work that demands sustained concentration.

Physical effects become more obvious as the session develops. Warmth can spread through the limbs, muscular tension may ease, and the urge to remain busy gradually decreases. At moderate amounts, this transition often creates a pleasant balance between mental enjoyment and bodily calm. Larger servings can shift much more decisively toward sedation, particularly for people with lower tolerance.

Modern Banana Pudding flower can test at fairly high THC levels, but there is no single breeder-issued percentage that defines every plant. Phenotype, cultivation, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology all affect cannabinoid results. Too much high-THC marijuana can produce dizziness, dry mouth, impaired memory, anxiety, or sleepiness even when the initial experience feels cheerful and manageable.
Medical Benefits

The progression from elevated mood into deeper physical relaxation has made Banana Pudding attractive to some medical cannabis consumers looking for evening relief without beginning with an immediately narcotic effect. Anecdotally, people may choose cultivars with this type of profile when dealing with discomfort, poor appetite, stress, or difficulty settling down late in the day.

Those uses should remain separate from proven medical claims. Banana Pudding itself has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials, and a strain name does not guarantee a particular medical outcome. Cannabis research more broadly suggests potential benefit from cannabinoids for some forms of chronic pain and nausea, but results vary considerably according to dose, cannabinoid ratio, route of administration, and individual response.

A high-THC phenotype may also work against the desired outcome. Someone seeking relaxation can instead experience anxiety or dizziness if the dose is excessive, while the later body heaviness may interfere with daytime activities. Medical marijuana consumers should therefore rely on batch-specific testing and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than assuming all Banana Pudding flower behaves identically.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Freshly opened flower often begins with banana, but the character is closer to slightly green banana peel than artificial banana candy. Sweetness follows quickly, sometimes suggesting sugar cookies or smooth vanilla-like dough. Citrus adds brightness, while earth, resin, and OG Kush form a heavier base beneath the sweeter top notes.

The flavor becomes more layered on the exhale. Green banana can linger beside cookie sweetness, then give way to citrus zest, mineral earth, peppery spice, and a Kush-like finish. Properly cured examples may develop a creamy impression even without literally tasting like pudding. That combination explains the name more convincingly than a simple banana aroma alone: fruit at the front, dessert sweetness in the middle, and deeper OG character underneath.

Documented commercial expressions have shown limonene, beta-caryophyllene, beta-myrcene, alpha-pinene, and alpha-humulene. Limonene fits the citrus brightness, while caryophyllene and humulene complement pepper, herbs, and earth. Myrcene can reinforce the deeper fruit and plant-like character, and pinene may contribute a faint fresh edge. Exact proportions vary from harvest to harvest, so these compounds should be viewed as documented possibilities rather than an immutable recipe.
Growing Information

Banana Pudding is better documented as finished flower and hash material than as a standardized commercial seed line with rigid cultivation specifications. Dying Breed Seeds did not leave behind a universally accepted chart listing flowering time, yield, height, and nutrient requirements for every phenotype. That makes observation especially important when growing seed-derived plants.

Most cultivation descriptions place flowering around eight to nine weeks, which is reasonable for genetics built around Banana OG and OG-influenced material. Plants generally develop enough lateral branching to benefit from topping or low-stress training, while late-flowering branches may require support as flowers gain weight. A balanced canopy is particularly useful because light penetration helps reduce airy lower growth and encourages more consistent resin development across the plant.

Trichome production is one of the strongest reasons to preserve a good phenotype. Banana Pudding has developed a reputation among solventless extract makers because selected plants can release substantial resin during washing. Heavy external trichome coverage does not automatically guarantee exceptional hash yield, since gland structure and separation matter as much as visible frost, but the strain has produced notable wash-friendly selections.

Dense mature flowers make airflow equally important. Relative humidity should be watched carefully late in bloom because moisture trapped inside compact buds can encourage botrytis even when the outside of the plant looks healthy. Removing weak interior shoots and maintaining space between major flowering branches can reduce stagnant pockets of air.

Nutrient demand depends strongly on phenotype. OG-leaning plants do not always appreciate aggressive feeding, so steadily increasing fertility according to plant response is generally safer than assuming the cannabis variety requires a heavy program. Excess nitrogen late in flowering can also delay maturation and interfere with the cleaner fruit-and-cookie expression that makes the strain attractive.

Outdoor growers should consider local autumn conditions more carefully than a universal harvest date. An eight-to-nine-week flowering phenotype may finish during early or mid-autumn after natural flowering begins, but latitude and climate can shift that window significantly. Dry weather during the final weeks is advantageous because mature resinous flowers can become dense.

Drying and curing have a major influence on the finished profile. Excessive heat can strip away the lighter banana and citrus compounds quickly, leaving a much more ordinary earthy Kush aroma. A slow, controlled dry followed by curing in stable conditions gives the sweet cookie, green banana, citrus, and OG components time to settle into a more coherent flavor.
FAQ
What is the genetics of Banana Pudding?

The original Dying Breed Seeds Banana Pudding is Banana OG × OG Eddy. Other cultivars using the same or similar name have been listed with GSC, Runtz, or other parents, so breeder identity matters when confirming the lineage.
Who bred Banana Pudding?

Dying Breed Seeds created the original version discussed here. The California breeder became known for fruit-forward and resin-heavy genetics, and Banana Pudding was subsequently used in additional breeding projects such as Banana OG BX1 and Banana Ringz.
What does Banana Pudding taste like?

The classic profile combines green banana, sugary cookie sweetness, citrus, earth, Kush, and mild spice. Some examples develop a creamy or vanilla-like quality after curing, while others lean more strongly toward banana peel and OG funk.
How strong is Banana Pudding?

Modern flower commonly reaches the 20% THC range and can test higher, but Dying Breed Seeds did not establish a single permanent THC percentage for the cultivar. Batch-specific laboratory testing is the best measure of actual potency.
Did Banana Pudding win a Cannabis Cup?

Banana Pudding concentrate entered by Apex won first place in the Sativa Concentrate category at the 2019 High Times Northern California Cannabis Cup. It also appeared among recognized concentrate entries during the same period, helping increase awareness of the genetics among extract consumers.
Final Thoughts on Banana Pudding

Banana Pudding works because its name only describes the surface. Beneath the dessert association is an OG-heavy California hybrid with a traceable Dying Breed Seeds pedigree, substantial resin production, and enough aromatic complexity to keep it from becoming a novelty banana strain .

Banana OG supplies the unmistakable fruit signature, while OG Eddy reinforces the Kush depth, sugary character, and physical weight. Together they produce flowers that can move from green banana and citrus into sweet cookie, earth, mineral resin, and spice. That contrast becomes even more pronounced after a careful cure.

The effects develop with similar layering. A cheerful, conversational beginning gradually gives way to physical ease and, with heavier consumption, pronounced relaxation. That progression makes the cultivar flexible at moderate doses but considerably more sedating once the amount increases.

Cultivators are most likely to value selected plants for resin quality, strong aromatic expression, and their potential for concentrate production. Although the original breeder did not leave a complete modern cultivation specification sheet, an approximately eight-to-nine-week flowering window, careful canopy management, strong late-flower airflow, and patient post-harvest handling fit the genetic background well.

Its 2019 High Times NorCal Cannabis Cup concentrate win further demonstrated what extract makers had already discovered: the cultivar can be much more than sweet-smelling flower. When the right phenotype brings together Banana OG fruit, sugary OG depth, and abundant resin, Banana Pudding becomes one of the more distinctive banana-themed hybrids of its generation.
